source_documents.title: Fluorescent Detection Probes for Hg2+ and Zn2+ with Schiff Base Structure Based on a Turn-On ESIPT–CHEF Mechanism

conditions_studied.media: THF, DCM, MeCN, DMF, DMSO, EA, MeOH, EtOH

reference_evidence_units.quote: Probe 3c only shows dual emission bands in DMF and DMSO (Figure 6), which is characteristic of a typical ESIPT process
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3c
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dual (enol + keto) emission, read by the authors as ESIPT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state spectra only; no time-resolved data.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with the maximum intensity observed at a 70% water fraction (Figure 7)
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3c
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission changes non-monotonically with water fraction, maximal at 70% water.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Aggregation is inferred, not characterised (no DLS/SEM).

reference_evidence_units.quote: these motions are significantly restricted, thereby suppressing non-radiative decay channels and leading to remarkable fluorescence enhancement
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 3a-3c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: MeOH or DMSO / water mixtures, aggregated
reference_evidence_units.statement: AIE-type enhancement attributed to restricted rotation/vibration of the diethylamino alkyl chains in the aggregate.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Interpretation only; the water-fraction curves are non-monotonic (decrease, rise, decrease) and no viscosity or rigid-matrix control is reported.

reference_evidence_units.quote: It can be observed that the LUMO energy level of the enol form is higher than that of the keto form.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 3a-3c and keto tautomers
reference_evidence_units.statement: Frontier orbital energies of enol vs keto forms are used to argue that ESIPT is favourable.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Ground-state orbital energies only; no excited-state proton-transfer profile.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This is likely because the coordination of compounds 3a–3c with the metal ions enhances the structural rigidity of the molecules while simultaneously suppressing C=N isomerization and the ESIPT process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 3a-3c with Hg2+/Zn2+
reference_evidence_units.conditions: DMF/H2O or DMSO/H2O with metal ions
reference_evidence_units.statement: Turn-on upon metal binding is attributed to rigidification, blocked C=N isomerization and blocked ESIPT (CHEF).
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Concerns the metal complexes, not the free probe that is the case input.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: AIE-like enhancement in water mixtures attributed to restricted rotation/vibration of the diethylamino chains; interpretation-level evidence only.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ESIPT is the paper's stated mechanism for the free probe; the support is limited to steady-state dual enol/keto emission in aprotic solvents and ground-state tautomer orbitals, with no time-resolved data or excited-state proton-transfer calculation.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: AIE-like enhancement in water mixtures attributed to restricted rotation/vibration of the diethylamino chains; interpretation-level evidence only.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The D-π-A design and ICT are mentioned only as design motivation; no ICT evidence for the emission.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: ESIPT is the paper's stated mechanism for the free probe; the support is limited to steady-state dual enol/keto emission in aprotic solvents and ground-state tautomer orbitals, with no time-resolved data or excited-state proton-transfer calculation.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.rationale: Aggregation is invoked only as motion restriction; no intermolecular electronic coupling discussed.

out_of_pool.mechanism: chelation-enhanced fluorescence (CHEF) of the metal complex, with blocked C=N isomerization and ESIPT
